sources.citation: Keïta, Boniface (1984). Le malinké de Kita (parler de Bindougouba): Esquisse phonologique et grammaticale et liste lexicale comparative. Mandenkan 8. pp. 1-131.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Language is not in the catalog and has no existing statements; the work describes tone in detail and contains no statement about stress, so it supplies no placement to compare. It does establish that the language is tonal (relevant if the catalog wants a tone-language flag).

sources.citation: Creissels, Denis. 2020. Grammaticalization in Manding. In W. Bisang & A. Malchukov (eds), Grammaticalization scenarios. De Gruyter Mouton. 695-727 (author's PDF).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: sec. 1.3.1 Phonology: 'Manding languages are tonal languages with complex systems of combinatory rules responsible for frequent discrepancies between underlying tones and surface tones (see for example Creissels 2009: 19-39 on the tonal system of Kita Maninka)'. No mention of stress; gives the page locator of the book's tone chapter.

sources.citation: Nikitina, Tatiana. 2012. Compte rendu: Denis Creissels, Le malinké de Kita: Un parler mandingue de l'ouest du Mali. Cologne: Rüdiger Köppe, 2009. Mandenkan 48: 123-127.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Reports that the grammar 'presents a detailed, meticulous study of Malinké tonology' built on a marked/unmarked binary tonal opposition (L marked, after Creissels & Grégoire 1993) with an underlying autosegmental level; tone notation marks only changes of tone; definite form is the citation form (pp.124-125).

sources.citation: Creissels, Denis. 2009. Les relatives corrélatives: le cas du malinké de Kita. Langages 174: 39-52 (author's PDF; DOI 10.3917/lang.174.0039).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Syntax only; notes that the definite is 'une modification tonale résultant de l'adjonction d'un ton bas sous-jacent au schème tonal lexical'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Keïta, Boniface. 1984. Le malinké de Kita (parler de Bindougouba). Esquisse phonologique et grammaticale et liste lexicale comparative. Mandenkan 8 (Automne 1984), 131 pp. (with a Présentation by Denis Creissels, p.1).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. I Phonologie (pp.5-22) opens with I.1 LES TONS (pp.5-14): tone is lexically and grammatically distinctive (p.5), five tone symbols needed (H, L, rising, H+downstep, rising+downstep, p.5), lowering of final H sequences after L (pp.6-8), L~rising alternation (p.8), definite marked by an underlying L (pp.9-10), phonetic partial raising of L (p.10), two main lexical tone classes: all-H vs initial-L-with-alternating-final (pp.10-11), tonal compactness (pp.13-14). I.4 (p.21): the syllable is the tone-bearing unit; no vowel length (p.14). The full scanned (133 PDF pp.) has zero hits for…

sources.citation: Creissels, Denis. 2009. Le malinké de Kita: Un parler mandingue de l'ouest du Mali. Mande Languages and Linguistics 9. Cologne: Rüdiger Köppe. 4+247 pp. ISBN 978-3-89645-078-4.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: The authoritative modern description; the tone system occupies pp.19-39 (per Creissels 2020) with an autosegmental marked-L analysis (per Nikitina 2012); the only place a statement on stress/accent vs tone in Kita Maninka would be expected. Named by the earlier scan as 'incl. tonal/accentual system' but never opened.

sources.citation: Vydrin(e), Valentin. 2008. Reinterpreting Manding grammar: Kita Maninka, viewed by Denis Creissels. Afrika und Übersee 90 (2008/09): 259-272 (HAL: 259-282).

sources.note: 14-page review article by the leading Mande tonologist discussing Creissels' 'new interpretations'; would report whether the book's tonal analysis involves any accentual/culminative element and would supersede the Nikitina review as a second-hand statement.

sources.citation: Creissels, Denis & Claire Grégoire. 1993. La notion de ton marqué dans l'analyse d'une opposition tonale binaire: le cas du mandingue. Journal of African Languages and Linguistics 14(2): 107-154.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: online with a university library login (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Theoretical basis of the Kita Maninka tone analysis (marked L vs unmarked); discusses whether Manding binary tone systems have accent-like (culminative) properties, which bears directly on a tone-vs-stress classification.
